newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys fall on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys fall on weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed, with nearby contracts under pressure from good growing weather in South America and commission house sales, pit traders said.
"If the (South American) weather holds, they are going to have a huge crop," said Victor Lespinasse, vice president with Dean Witter brokerage in Chicago.
Trading volume was light ahead of the New Year's holiday on Wednesday when the exchange will be closed, traders said.
In late trade, Griffin Trading sold 2 million bushels March, which pushed the market to fresh session lows, traders said.

January stayed lower most of the session, under modest pressure from spread trade spurred by deliveries. The CBOT reported deliveries of 650,000 bushels against January on first notice day, trader said.
Cargill spread one million March/January, pit sources said.
CBOT soybeans closed down 3-3/4 cents per bushel to up 3-1/2, with January down 3-3/4 at $6.90-1/2 and March down 2-3/4 at $6.87-3/4.
On the day, Cargill sold one million bushels July and bought 1.5 million March. Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov bought 1.5 million March and FIMAT sold one million bushels March.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, below the 50,644 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
